business_problem: iFood needed to stop hand-managing Kafka capacity and batch pipelines so it could decouple thousands of services, move food-ordering data in real time, and make analytics and delivery tracking available across the business.
solution_summary: iFood replaced a managed-but-still-heavy Kafka setup with Confluent Cloud so it could fully decouple its food-ordering architecture and expand real-time data use across the company. The platform now carries streaming data pipelines between 2,000 microservices, feeds an AWS data lake for analytics and machine learning, and ingests delivery-driver geolocation streams that power real-time customer tracking. iFood also uses fully managed ksqlDB to aggregate and transform live streams, including per-second order monitoring that helps teams understand platform health as transactions occur. Stream Governance and Schema Registry give developers a safer way to connect new systems while preserving compatibility and traceability as data moves. Over time, Confluent has become a central nervous system for 700 applications, letting teams consume and react to enriched operational data without building or maintaining low-level Kafka tooling.

data_flow: Orders, delivery-driver geolocation, and application events stream through Confluent Cloud to downstream microservices, ksqlDB aggregates and transforms the data in motion, and enriched outputs land in an AWS data lake and customer-facing tracking experiences.
business_outcome: iFood improved real-time order visibility, reduced platform operations burden, gave teams self-service access to live data, and scaled a streaming backbone that now supports hundreds of applications and millions of orders.
